initial.name: ask_user_question
initial.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

initial.name: bash
initial.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: dsh_im_return_file
initial.description: Register a readable file or generated image for delivery through the current IM conversation after this turn. Requires an active IM delivery consumer; in Web, Desktop, or CLI conversations use the host present tool if available. Existing and newly created files are both valid. Success means queued, not sent; do not claim the user has received the file.

path.description: Absolute path, or a path relative to the current workspace.

initial.name: edit
initial.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: edit_video
initial.description: Edit existing local videos without generating new media or spending model credits. Order clips as supplied, optionally trim each start/end in seconds, normalize and concatenate them, and optionally trim the final length. Input files must be readable inside this workspace or an owned generated-video project. Returns a background job_id; wait for the real final_path, then call present and include the artifact link. This performs ordered cuts and joins; it does not synthesize unseen footage, music, subtitles, or effects. If current user-supplied chat attachments are outside the workspace, first copy only those read-authorized attachments into this workspace with existing file tools, then edit the copied paths.

clips.description: Local clip paths in final playback order, with optional per-clip trim positions. Copy current user-supplied, read-authorized chat attachments from outside the workspace into the workspace with existing file tools before passing their copied paths.

total_duration_seconds.description: Optional final duration after assembling clips; cannot exceed the available trimmed footage.

initial.name: exit_plan_mode
initial.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

initial.name: find_dsh_plugin
initial.description: Search GitHub for DeepSeek Harness plugins (public `dsh-plugin` topic), ranked by stars. Returns descriptions and ready-to-run `dsh plugin add` install commands. Use when the user wants a capability DSH does not currently have, or asks what plugins exist. Plugins are third-party code — advise reviewing the source and pinning a commit. Falls back to keyword matches from the curated awesome-dsh-plugin list when GitHub search is rate limited or unreachable; the note states which source was used.

query.description: Keywords describing the capability, e.g. "wechat notifications", "TUI", "跨会话记忆"

lang.description: Preferred description language for curated entries (e.g. 'en', 'zh'). Defaults to 'en'.

initial.name: generate_image
initial.description: Generate images or edit reference images through the signed-in account relay, save every result into the artifacts directory, and return the paths. For pending or unknown results, never resubmit this tool: use query_image_task with the original plan_id and operation_id when a task_id was received. Without a task_id, retain the unknown outcome and reconcile the original request before any paid retry. For image-to-image requests, pass the current-chat user attachment or an authorized workspace image in reference_images. Which image models exist, and what each one accepts, is the deployment’s own answer: ask for a model only when the user names one. For failed operations, give users only a safe Simplified Chinese summary based on the observed failure category; connection failures and timeouts do not establish whether the cause is local, network, platform or upstream. Distinguish confirmed request or media validation, permission, rate limiting, service HTTP 5xx and upstream task failures; unknown causes remain unconfirmed; never repeat raw HTTP responses, diagnostic JSON, error codes, stacks, internal paths or credentials. Keep actionable guidance for confirmed sign-in, product-credit, file-validation and cancellation failures. When submission or billing outcome is unknown, check existing tasks and artifacts first; do not immediately retry or automatically resubmit. Preserve real tool results. This restriction does not prevent software or code diagnostics explicitly requested by the user.

plan_id.description: Explicit update_creation_plan id for this generation. Also provide exactly one of shot_id or asset_id.

shot_id.description: Exact shot id in the explicit plan; never guess a latest project.

asset_id.description: Exact image asset id in plan_id, including a video plan. Mutually exclusive with shot_id. Creates or reconstructs this source asset, not a finished shot.

model.description: Optional image model id such as gpt-image-2. Defaults to the first image model the deployment serves for this account.

size.description: Optional output size from the selected model’s published menu. yunshu-internal-gpt-image-2 accepts aspect-ratio strings only when its live catalog declares them, never pixel dimensions; use resolution for its independent 1k, 2k or 4k tier. An undeclared value is refused before generation.

resolution.description: Optional named output tier, only when declared by the chosen model. yunshu-internal-gpt-image-2 accepts 1k, 2k or 4k and defaults to 1k; this is independent from pixel size.

count.description: How many images to render, within the model’s limit (usually 1–4).

reference_images.description: Reference images for editing: current-chat user image attachment ids or their exact read-only paths, readable PNG/JPEG/WebP files inside the current workspace, uploaded ma_ ids, or real generated image output ids/paths owned by the same explicit plan_id. Other-chat attachments, unrelated local paths and URLs are refused.

initial.name: generate_video
initial.description: Compatibility single-clip generation through the account relay. Read list_video_models first. Prefer generate_video_project for new video requests, including a single clip: its background job exposes queue and generation progress without holding chat open. Do not write submission, polling or download scripts or probe invalid paid durations. For story direction, character/reference continuity, dialogue or subtitles, use the yunshu-video-director skill. For a complete video such as 40 seconds or automatic assembly, always use generate_video_project; several camera beats may fit one clip. Accepted work that outlasts this foreground wait returns pending: query_video_task reads its original receipt, never generate again. Edit existing clips with edit_video. Only declared duration, resolution, ratio, frames and references are accepted. For failed operations, give users only a safe Simplified Chinese summary based on the observed failure category; connection failures and timeouts do not establish whether the cause is local, network, platform or upstream. Distinguish confirmed request or media validation, permission, rate limiting, service HTTP 5xx and upstream task failures; unknown causes remain unconfirmed; never repeat raw HTTP responses, diagnostic JSON, error codes, stacks, internal paths or credentials. Keep actionable guidance for confirmed sign-in, product-credit, file-validation and cancellation failures. When submission or billing outcome is unknown, check existing tasks and artifacts first; do not immediately retry or automatically resubmit. Preserve real tool results. This restriction does not prevent software or code diagnostics explicitly requested by the user.

plan_id.description: Explicit update_creation_plan id for this generation. Also provide shot_id.

shot_id.description: Exact shot id in the explicit plan; never guess a latest project.

prompt.description: What the video should show. Before calling, script user-delegated narrative or dialogue scenes with stable character ids, language, brief exact lines and their timing, identifying on-screen speakers versus narration; preserve user-supplied wording. Do not reduce a story requiring voices to a music montage. Respect silent/no-dialogue requests and do not add dialogue or subtitles to unrelated nonverbal videos. Include requested lip-sync and subtitle requirements. These request native model generation, not separate speech, lip-sync or subtitle processing; verify the rendered result before claiming they are met.

model.description: Optional video model id such as MiniMax-H3. Defaults to the first video model the deployment serves for this account.

duration_seconds.description: Clip length in seconds; only values the chosen model declares are accepted.

resolution.description: Output resolution such as 768P or 2K, when the model offers choices.

ratio.description: Aspect ratio such as 16:9 or 9:16; adaptive inherits it from the reference media.

audio.description: Optional requested audio state. Sent as a switch only when the chosen model declares one; fixed native audio accepts only its declared state. An audio stream does not verify dialogue, lip-sync or subtitles.

frame_images.description: Optional stored ids (ma_…) used as first/last frame.

reference_images.description: Optional stored ids (ma_…) used as multimodal subject/style references, when the model supports them.

reference_videos.description: Optional stored ids (ma_…) used as a reference video, when the model supports video-to-video.

reference_audios.description: Optional uploaded ma_ audio ids or workspace WAV/MP3 paths, when the model supports audio references. First copy a user-supplied, read-authorized chat attachment outside the workspace into the workspace using existing file tools; do not copy unrelated files. References do not guarantee copied speech, matching mouth movements or subtitles.

initial.name: generate_video_project
initial.description: Default fixed background workflow for every new chat video, including a single short clip and a finished video longer than one model clip. For a simple single-clip brief without an explicit duration, call this tool directly with prompt and any requested model or references; omit total_duration_seconds so the Host resolves actual defaults in one call. Do not load directing skills, write a long storyboard or call list_video_models first for that simple case. For explicit timing or complex plans, read list_video_models for actual controls; never discover support by paid retries or silently replace an explicitly named model. Use the yunshu-video-director skill for story, character/reference continuity, dialogue and subtitles, then call this native workflow; do not write polling, download or assembly scripts or manually repeat generate_video for each visual cut. One paid clip can contain several camera beats. For requests such as a 40-second video, plan the fewest supported clips (for a 15-second limit: 15+15+10, or three 15-second clips trimmed to 40), generate independent clips with gateway-approved bounded parallelism using the signed-in account, then normalize, trim, and join them in timeline order. Older gateways remain serial; the API owns shared account capacity. Do not launch a separate agent or generation-tool call for every clip. For a catalog with H3 single clips limited to 4–15 seconds, 60 seconds means four 15-second clips, never one 30-second clip. All local tools and every request are checked before billing. Returns a background job_id and durable project_id; read job_output at measured intervals for queued/generating progress and call present on the completed final_path. A busy response without an accepted task id is unknown, not confirmed queue admission. Use job_kill when the user stops; accepted provider tasks may continue billing. A query deadline retains task ids for explicit resume, never a fresh submission. Never claim completion before the job reports a saved final_path. If a current user-supplied chat attachment is outside the workspace, first copy that read-authorized attachment into this workspace with the existing file tools, then pass the copied path; do not copy unrelated files.

plan_id.description: Explicit update_creation_plan id. Also supply shot_ids in generation order.

shot_ids.description: Exact shot ids belonging to plan_id, one per actual supported model clip and in the saved timeline order. Multiple visual cuts may share one paid clip; do not create an unsupported paid clip for each camera beat.

prompt.description: The complete video brief, visual continuity, story, and desired editing. Before calling, script user-delegated narrative or dialogue scenes with stable character ids, language and brief exact lines, identifying on-screen speakers versus narration; preserve user-supplied wording. Assign each line and its timing to a shot in shot_prompts. Do not reduce a story requiring voices to a music montage. Respect silent/no-dialogue requests and do not add dialogue or subtitles to unrelated nonverbal videos. Include requested lip-sync and subtitle requirements. These request native model generation, not separate speech, lip-sync or subtitle processing; verify the rendered result before claiming they are met.

total_duration_seconds.description: Desired final length in whole seconds; this may exceed the model single-clip limit. For a simple single clip with no plan or explicit shot arrays, omit to use the selected model’s actual default duration. The Host reads the real catalog itself; no separate list_video_models call is needed. Required for explicit plans and shot arrays; never omit a user-specified duration.

shot_prompts.description: Exact shot briefs, one per planned clip. With plan_id and shot_ids, omit to use each saved shot’s scene, camera, action, prompt, exact dialogue/subtitles and associated character definitions without another model call. Explicit values remain verbatim. Otherwise allocate delegated narrative lines and timing to stable speakers, distinguishing on-screen speech from narration. Respect silent/no-dialogue requests.

shot_durations_seconds.description: Exact model-supported whole seconds per clip, in shot_ids or shot_prompts order. Their sum must equal total_duration_seconds. When omitted for an explicit creation plan, use its saved shot durations; do not silently change timeline timing.

model.description: Exact id from list_video_models. Preserve an explicitly requested model; never silently switch it. Otherwise choose an available account model using its returned duration, dimension and audio declarations.

audio.description: Optional requested audio state from list_video_models, not a capability probe. Sent as a switch only when the chosen model declares one; fixed native audio accepts only its declared state. No switch does not mean silent output; an undeclared audio state remains unknown. Do not blindly send true, and do not promise speech, lip-sync, subtitles or silence without checking the media.

frame_images.description: Existing uploaded ma_ first/last frame ids or workspace image paths. For a user-supplied chat attachment outside the workspace, first copy the read-authorized attachment into the workspace with existing file tools and pass its copied path.

reference_images.description: Shared uploaded ma_ subject/style image ids or workspace image paths used by every shot. With plan_id, each shot’s saved image materials and character references are added only to that shot; do not duplicate unrelated character references here. For a user-supplied chat attachment outside the workspace, first copy the read-authorized attachment into the workspace with existing file tools and pass its copied path.

reference_videos.description: Existing uploaded ma_ video reference ids or workspace video paths. For a user-supplied chat attachment outside the workspace, first copy the read-authorized attachment into the workspace with existing file tools and pass its copied path.

reference_audios.description: Existing uploaded ma_ audio reference ids or workspace WAV/MP3 paths, only when the chosen model supports audio references. For a user-supplied chat attachment outside the workspace, first copy the read-authorized attachment into the workspace with existing file tools and pass its copied path. A reference does not guarantee copied speech, matching mouth movements or subtitles.

initial.name: get_creation_plan
initial.description: Read the complete structured plan owned by this account, chat and workspace before revising it. Returns the exact planning fields accepted by update_creation_plan, including stable character, asset and shot ids. Preserve all unrelated entries when updating. This read neither generates media, resumes tasks nor spends credits; it excludes provider requests and credentials.

initial.name: get_goal
initial.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

initial.name: ipollowork_video_validate
initial.description: Validate the editable HyperFrames video belonging to one DeepSeek Harness workspace and conversation session.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

initial.name: list_video_models
initial.description: Read the signed-in account’s current video models and exact generation parameters without submitting or charging for generation. Call when planning explicit model controls or paid clip lengths. A simple single-clip request can directly call generate_video_project without total_duration_seconds: the Host resolves actual model defaults in the same call. Use exact ids, durations by resolution, size strings, reference limits and audio_output; do not infer audio from a missing switch or use display names as ids. This catalog does not report live upstream capacity. For queued work use the background generate_video_project workflow, including one clip.

initial.name: present
initial.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

initial.name: query_image_task

With both original plan_id and operation_id, query that accepted task and save completed outputs. If the original submission has no task id, retain its unknown outcome and reconcile the original request instead of generating again. This restriction does not prevent software or code diagnostics explicitly requested by the user.

plan_id.description: Original retained creation plan id; required when querying one operation.

operation_id.description: Original generation operation id. Omit to list unresolved receipts without starting queries.

With both original plan_id and operation_id, query that accepted task and save completed outputs. Distinguish confirmed request or media validation, permission, rate limiting, service HTTP 5xx and upstream task failures; unknown causes remain unconfirmed; never repeat raw HTTP responses, diagnostic JSON, error codes, stacks, internal paths or credentials. Keep actionable guidance for confirmed sign-in, product-credit, file-validation and cancellation failures. When submission or billing outcome is unknown, check existing tasks and artifacts first; do not immediately retry or automatically resubmit. Preserve real tool results. plan_id.description: Original retained creation plan id; required when querying one operation.

operation_id.description: Original generation operation id. Omit to list unresolved receipts without starting queries.

initial.name: read
initial.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

initial.name: read_image
initial.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

initial.name: resume_video_project
initial.description: Explicitly continue a retained project for the same account, workspace, and chat. Reuse saved clips and query already known provider task ids before submitting any remaining never-submitted clips. Unknown or failed clips block new submissions, while other already accepted task ids remain recoverable for download. Never repeat unknown or failed submissions, and refuse a second live run. Local cancellation cannot cancel already accepted upstream billing.

initial.name: schedule_create
initial.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters, shown on the task card and in task lists.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

initial.name: schedule_delete
initial.description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or inactive. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

initial.name: schedule_list
initial.description: List the active reminders in the current session.

initial.name: schedule_update
initial.description: Change a reminder in place, keeping its id. Supply a new title, prompt, or at most one timing parameter; omitted fields keep their stored values. To change a relative delay, create a new reminder.

title.description: New task name of at most 120 characters.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

initial.name: skill
initial.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

initial.name: subagent_fork
initial.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

initial.name: todo_write

While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

initial.name: univer_api
initial.description: Look up the bundled, version-matched Univer Facade API. Use find when no relevant class or API label is known. Use show for a known class, type, or exact Class.member API label; to inspect APIs on a known class, show the class itself. Find is case-insensitive. Each query runs independently and returns its own matches: queries are never combined as AND, and find does not interpret intent.

action.description: find discovers unknown class or API labels; show documents a known class, type, or exact Class.member label. Show a known class to inspect its APIs.

queries.description: For find, API-name keywords or identifier fragments such as conditionalFormat. For show, known class, type, or exact Class.member labels such as FRange or FRange.setValue. Find queries are case-insensitive and independent, not AND terms.

unit.description: Optional find-only Unit filter; shared APIs remain included.

limit.description: Find-only maximum matches per query. Prefer 10 or fewer.

initial.name: univer_compile_svg

source.description: Workspace-relative or absolute SVG source path.

unitId.description: Explicit Slide Unit id from univer_status.

mode.description: Replace the page contents by default, or add the SVG as an overlay.

initial.name: univer_execute
initial.description: Execute Univer Facade JavaScript and commit mutations to a draft agent worktree. Use code only for a small snippet and codeFile for multiline or reusable code. Provide exactly one source. Explicitly return readback values; bare expressions and console.log do not populate value. Read-only code creates no revision.

code.description: Inline Facade code; use codeFile for multiline code. Mutually exclusive with codeFile.

codeFile.description: Workspace-relative or absolute multiline Facade JavaScript body file. Mutually exclusive with code.

name.description: Required non-empty Unit name for create.

initial.description: Create or transition an isolated Univer worktree. Actions: create, ready, reopen, merge, or discard. Merge and discard require user approval.

worktreeId.description: Required for every action except create.

initial.name: update_creation_plan
initial.description: Create or explicitly revise the structured plan for a chat image or video: stable characters and their appearance, source materials, ordered shots, camera, actions, exact dialogue and subtitles. Use the returned plan_id and the exact shot ids in generate_image/generate_video or shot_ids in generate_video_project. Never associate a generation with a guessed latest project. Planning does not generate media or spend credits. Character/material descriptions and dialogue are requirements, not verified generation results. Preserve user wording and silent/nonverbal requests. Revisions supply the complete plan and cannot remove shots with existing generation records.

source_path_or_asset_id.description: Existing real path or uploaded asset id; use an empty string for an asset that has not been generated. Never invent a path.

initial.name: update_goal
initial.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

initial.name: video_project_status
initial.description: Read a durable video project owned by this account, workspace, and chat. This does not restart generation or spend credits. After an app restart, an interrupted project is a saved record, not a live job. Inspect clip_paths and task_ids before explicitly resuming.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

initial.name: working_directory
initial.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

initial.name: write
initial.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
